messages.author: 5fc34a138d2dc378
messages.subject: Replicating NewHybid runs
parts:
Hi Arthur,

I was wondering if there is a function to replicate the random sampling of alleles (the 200 used in analysis) for NewHybrids in DartR. I would like to randomly choose 200 alleles from my dataset, say 100 times, to show that the results are constant.

Regards,
James

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: Replicating NewHybid runs
parts:
gl.nhybrids(gl, outfile = "nhyb.txt", outpath = tempdir(), p0 = NULL,
  p1 = NULL, threshold = 0, method = "random", plot = TRUE,
  pprob = 0.95, nhyb.directory = NULL, BurnIn = 10000,
  sweeps = 10000, GtypFile = "TwoGensGtypFreq.txt",
  AFPriorFile = NULL, PiPrior = "Jeffreys", ThetaPrior = "Jeffreys",
  verbose = 2)

method="random" should do the trick, provided you have more than 200 loci fixed between your parentals. 
If you do not have 200 fixed loci between your parentals, not sure. I think it will pick the fixed ones each time
and randomize the selection of the remainder.

Then you will have to run it 100 times in a loop, to yield 100 outfiles, then run each of them in NewHybrids, then create a consensus of the 
results.

This will be a bit easier if you run New Hybrids from within dartR, but people have had variable success with this.

Hope this helps.

A
